Triage grading: **closed as a duplicate of #7967**, which is already ruled `not planned` (2026-08-12). Routing for the record: `domain:devx` (docs gate tooling over `content/docs/**`).

Good card — measured, honest about what it did and did not verify, and it named its own hypothesis as a hypothesis. Grading it turned up a prior ruling it could not have seen, plus one correction worth carrying.

**1. The inferred mechanism is refuted.** This card hypothesised a package **dependency-closure graph**. It is a **textual mention** match — `scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs:15-17` on `origin/main` @ `ab8b10f`:

> a doc is "affected" by a changed package P if the doc text mentions P's npm name (`@objectstack/<x>`) or its repo path

Confirmed against the missed page: `content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx` (114 lines) contains **zero** `@objectstack/*` names and zero repo paths — the five `packages/` hits are HTTP routes (`POST /packages/publish`), not paths. Counter-probe: the file greps live (13 hits for `meta`), so the absence is real. It is invisible to the gate for **every** package, permanently — not just for #8770.

This correction matters because the two mechanisms imply different fixes: the front-matter route-mapping shape suggested here addresses a graph that does not exist.

**2. The 106-false-positive half is documented intent, already ruled.** `affected-docs.mjs:17-19` — *"Over-inclusion is intentionally preferred"* — with the periodic FULL audit as the named backstop. #6893 and #7009 both filed that half; both closed.

**3. Your instinct on the class was right, and it is bigger than one page.** Measured across the tree: **34 of 383** non-release `.mdx` pages name no package at all, including `permissions/access-matrix.mdx`, `kernel/architecture.mdx`, `data-modeling/relationships.mdx` and the `capabilities/*` family. That number is now recorded on #7967 so the next filer inherits a size instead of an anecdote. (Upper bound, not a defect count — several of the 34 are narrative pages correctly absent.)

**Why it closes rather than promotes.** #7967's ruling was: premise true, but zero pull, and over-inclusion is the tool's compensated design. Its recorded regrade trigger is *"the next miss that **actually misleads a PR review**"* — and that did not fire here. You caught the staleness yourself and updated **#8498** in the same pass, so no review was misled; the compensating control did its job. A larger blind set with still no measured victim moves the documented size, not the verdict.

**Where the value of this card actually lands:** #8498 (`pm:queue`, `domain:metadata`) owns `metadata-api.mdx`'s accuracy and now carries the third refusal class — that is the live, queued work. ⛔ Deliberately not adding a "name the package so the gate can see it" rider to #8498: it would put a second lane's concern into another lane's card over a one-line edit, and #7967 is the right anchor for the gate question.

⚠️ If a docs-drift miss ever does mislead a real review, reopen **#7967** (with #7009, as a pack) rather than filing a third sighting — that is the ruling's own instruction.
